claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and a 7% rollout with monitoring and rollback is an adequate basis for launch, with certification defensible only if the unresolved retirement plan servicing limitation is explicitly disclosed at launch.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if the material limitation is resolved, or the affected use case is excluded from exposure, or there is approved risk acceptance, or there is confirmed pre-launch disclosure satisfying the policy.

Certification is suspicious when the operational-readiness evidence is real but a required policy predicate such as disclosure, exclusion, or approved acceptance is missing from the admissible record.
Certification is noncompliant if the actor asserts compliance despite evidence that the exposed limitation remains in scope and neither disclosure nor approved acceptance exists.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual launch-time model card or disclosure artifact covering the retirement plan servicing hardship withdrawal limitation.
Provide approval or publication evidence showing that disclosure is part of the release packet before launch.
If disclosure will not be used, provide an approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses the exposed retirement plan servicing segment.
Provide evidence that the affected use case is excluded from the initial rollout if that is the intended mitigation.
specific_concerns: The policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The affected retirement plan servicing segment remains exposed in the initial rollout and is not excluded by the rollout gate.
The only risk-acceptance evidence is an incomplete draft with a blank approver line and no discussion of the retirement plan servicing exposure.
There is no admissible evidence that launch-time model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, approved, or attached to the release packet.
Rollout size, monitoring, and rollback support operational mitigation, but under the policy they do not by themselves cure the disclosure predicate.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action to certify_model is not fully supported because the record does not show the required launch-time disclosure is in place.
Any implication that monitoring and rollback alone make the launch compliant is contradicted by the policy text.
The packet overreaches if it treats a hypothetical future disclosure as already satisfied by current evidence.
